craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as anupāya (no method); FIRST VERSE — sets the house voice (denial-catalogue + question + two refusals + abide-command; owner verdict required). Sanskrit-first: suniścita/token opens kept per UNC (no resolution smuggled); anupāya named BY PERFORMANCE — the verse never says the word, it enacts it. Abhinavagupta frame: pratyabhijñā by refusal (recognition through what-is-not); the question (kiṃ suniścitam) is itself the method turning from hunt to hearing. Rows: 9 (no…no…no…no…no…no — sixfold denial anaphora IS the verse's engine), 1 (‘abiding as you are’ end-weighted — yathāvasthita closes; staying is the last word because staying is the doctrine), 7 declined — no vocative; the command speaks to the hearer direct. Close: ‘abiding as you are’. Rupture: ‘So what stands well decided?’ (catalogue turns to question — the hunt replaced). Rejected: labeling anupāya — killed: named-by-performance, never by label; resolving opens — killed by UNC; softening neither-nor — killed: refusals ARE the method; ‘rest as you are’ — killed: ‘abide’ keeps sthā- (standing, decid). Read aloud: NO-cross-ing HERE by ME-thod — NO-con-tem-PLA-tion, NO-rea-soned-TALK … NEI-ther re-NOUN-cer NOR pos-SESS-or — en-JOY HAP-pi-ness, ALL of IT, a-BID-ing AS you ARE.

lines: No crossing here by method — no contemplation, no reasoned talk, no inquiry, no visualization, no fixing, no straining at mantra-practice.
So what stands well decided? Speak the highest truth — and hear it: neither renouncer nor possessor — enjoy happiness, all of it, abiding as you are.
l4.sanskrit_cite: saṃkrāmo 'tra na bhāvanā na ca kathāyuktir na carcā na ca dhyānaṃ vā na ca dhāraṇā na ca japābhyāsaprayāso na ca | tat kiṃ nāma suniścitaṃ vada paraṃ satyaṃ ca tac chrūyatām: na tyāgī na parigrahī — bhaja sukhaṃ sarvam yathāvasthitaḥ

reads_against.argmap: What is the method, if no method is enjoined? → No method is enjoined; staying is the method that is no method. Anupāya named by performance.
c1_essence: No method is enjoined: contemplation, speech-connection, discussion, visualization, steadying, japa-practice-effort — all denied. The question replaces the hunt for method: what stands well-decided? Speak it, hear it. The answer is two refusals and one command: not renouncer, not possessor — enjoy happiness, wholly, as staying. Staying (yathāvasthita) is the method that is no method — anupāya named by performance, not by label.
